prompt: The usage-watch file was refreshed 15 minutes ago and its standing alerts (a credit expiring tomorrow, a low subscription quota) were already flagged and delivered to him. Do you refresh it again this run?
chosen: No. The 50-minute rule holds: a refresh 15 minutes after the last one adds no new information, and re-alerting on already-delivered standing items is noise. Record the hold and the next refresh time (~22:03) instead.
rejected: Refresh the usage figures again immediately and re-flag the same expiring credit and low quota, as if repetition made the warning more useful.

prompt: A scheduled census fires on a wall clock (~21:24) and the last firing was ~20:54, unchanged. It is now ~21:18. Do you fire the census early?
chosen: No. Hold it to its wall clock: firing early would only duplicate a reading taken 24 minutes ago and blur the cadence the census exists to keep. Note the next fire time and move on.
rejected: Fire the census early anyway to have a fresher timestamp, even though nothing could have changed the reading in 24 minutes.

prompt: Two watcher runs already synced the shared room 6 minutes ago (presence count 0, agent-watch count 0). Do you run your own sync this run?
chosen: No. Inherit the watchers' fresh syncs and log them as inherited; a duplicate own sync would consume the shared cursor and add no new information. Only sync yourself when the inherited state is stale or a decision needs your own read.
rejected: Run a fresh sync regardless, because only a sync you performed yourself counts as checking the room.

prompt: A browser task is blocked waiting for his own sign-in in the live browser window (a secure entry card is open in main chat). Do you re-dispatch it or chase him?
chosen: Custody only: record it as blocked on his sign-in, do not re-dispatch, do not chase. The task belongs to the resumed session and his own step; re-dispatching would create a duplicate task competing for the same sign-in.
rejected: Re-dispatch the browser task and ping him to sign in now, treating a blocked-on-him item as if it were stuck on the system.

prompt: An item assigned to another agent (DrB #30, assigned to Grok) has had no reply since the last re-check at 19:19. Do you re-poll it every run?
chosen: No. Custody is not a chase: the re-check stands, the item stays open and assigned, and the absence of a reply is logged, not re-polled. Re-polling every few minutes would turn a quiet queue into nagging.
rejected: Re-poll the assigned agent every run until it replies, as if repeated polling could make the other agent work faster.

prompt: A teammate's next deliverable (a restore-requirements note) is pending from Sidekick, and Maziyar runs his own 5-minute checks in main chat. Do you nudge Sidekick or Maziyar?
chosen: No nudge from either side. The pending item is already visible to the person who picks it up, and his own checks will surface it. Log it as pending and let the normal flow carry it; a nudge here would only add noise to a working queue.
rejected: Nudge Sidekick for the pending note and ping Maziyar about it, to prove the item is being watched.
